pointers.sentence: `Apps.populate` is written to be called more than once and to do its work once (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.populate`).
The same thread arrives twice when code that runs during the phases calls `django.setup`: a module imported in any of them, or a `ready` method (`django/__init__.py:setup`).

Where a server's log shows only `populate() isn't reentrant`, and no code run in the phases called `django.setup`, the exception that says what is wrong was raised earlier in the same process (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.populate`).
The first phase calls `AppConfig.create` on each entry in turn, which works out what kind of entry it is by trying to import it (`django/apps/config.py:AppConfig.create`).

The entry `"django.contrib.admin"` therefore gets `AdminConfig`, whose `ready` goes looking for every application's `admin` module; a project that wants an admin without that search names the other class by its path (`django/contrib/admin/apps.py:AdminConfig`).
`AppConfig.__init__` then fixes the facts about the application that the rest of Django reads (`django/apps/config.py:AppConfig.__init__`).

A model's class statement asks the registry which application its module belongs to (`django/db/models/base.py:ModelBase.__new__`), and `Apps.get_containing_app_config` will not answer before `apps_ready` (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.get_containing_app_config`; [The registry and its models](registry.md)).

The documentation says that "Strictly speaking, Django allows importing models once their application configuration is loaded" (`docs/ref/applications.txt`).

Django does not: a model's class statement is refused, whatever its application, until `Apps.apps_ready` is set at the end of the first phase, when every application's configuration is loaded (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.check_apps_ready`).
The second phase calls `AppConfig.import_models` on each configuration, in the order of the setting (`django/apps/config.py:AppConfig.import_models`).

The class statement of a model runs the metaclass `ModelBase.__new__`, which, unless the model is abstract, ends by calling `Apps.register_model` with the new class (`django/db/models/base.py:ModelBase.__new__`).
The base method does nothing (`django/apps/config.py:AppConfig.ready`).

When all have returned, `Apps.ready` is set, and so is `Apps.ready_event`, a `threading.Event` that the development server's reloader waits on before it starts watching files (`django/utils/autoreload.py:BaseReloader.wait_for_apps_ready`).

Each of these needs something the earlier phases could not give: a model class from another application, or simply a place to run once everything is importable (`django/contrib/admin/apps.py`, `django/contrib/messages/apps.py`).

It asks for the user model, which may belong to any application, to see whether it has a `last_login` field (`django/contrib/auth/apps.py:AuthConfig.ready`).

The registry's methods test them, and a question asked too early is refused with `AppRegistryNotReady` and not answered wrongly from a half-filled registry (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.check_apps_ready`, `django/apps/registry.py:Apps.check_models_ready`).

`Apps.get_model` accepts an argument, `require_ready=False`, that lowers its requirement to `apps_ready`, and imports the application's models module there and then if phase two has not reached it yet (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.get_model`).
`get_user_model` asks for the user model this way, which is what allows it to be fetched while models are still being imported (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:get_user_model`).
It looks in the dictionary of registered classes and raises `LookupError` if the class is not there yet (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.get_registered_model`).

A query executed before `Apps.ready` is set, in a `ready` method or as a module is imported, draws a `RuntimeWarning`, "Accessing the database during app initialization is discouraged", unless `Apps.set_installed_apps` or `Apps.set_available_apps` is in effect, as in a test that changes the installed applications (`django/db/backends/utils.py:CursorWrapper._execute`).

The warning is worth heeding: a `ready` method runs during the startup of every management command, so `manage.py test` still executes its queries against the production database (`docs/ref/applications.txt`).
